scope.ageInterpretation: Official stage window, with attainment referenced to stage end; not a claim that identical performance is due at every age or grade.

coverageMeaning: Authoring coverage judgments, not learner mastery or a conversion of suggestive outcomes into mandates.

contributions.topicName: Using objects to model real problems
contributions.contribution: Quantity situations represented and answered with objects, drawings or simple number sentences.
Shape distinctions justified through observable attributes.
Physical attributes measured using suitable standard units.

records.rationale: These existing claims contribute directly to the broad goal in its number, geometry and measurement strands. Their conjunction is not a certification of the complete stage goal.
remainingConditions: Integration across the whole mathematical domain and the unresolved competency conditions below remain open; child-code links alone do not prove goal attainment.

contributions.contribution: Two-attribute classification using intersections, cells and subgroup questions.

records.rationale: The complete claim, evidence and assessment cover simultaneous criteria and the relationships between groups. Its two-way tables and Carroll diagrams supply subgroups rather than merely single-attribute sorting.

contributions.contribution: Repeating cores identified, made, continued and translated across everyday objects, movements, shapes and number representations.
Additive growth or decrease recognised, described and constructed with numbers, objects or shapes.

records.rationale: Together these claims cover recognising and carrying out simple repeating and growing structures. Everyday objects and movements are already in the claims, so contextual transfer does not require a new country-specific claim.

contributions.contribution: Unit-step sequence in both directions through the required two-digit range.
Equal-step counting includes the five-step and ten-step strands.

records.rationale: The sequence and stated skip-counting claims directly address part of the performance. The misleading title of the second topic was not used as its scope: its description includes three step sizes.
remainingConditions: The twenty-step performance/example must still be demonstrated; it is not explicit in the selected evidence. This is not a finding of a separate missing counting claim, and does not justify a new numerical-step topic.

contributions.contribution: Place-value comparisons and ordered arrangements include all two-digit values.

records.rationale: The claim reaches beyond the required number range, but its recorded examples and assessment explicitly exercise increasing arrangements. A broader range is not a separate reason for a duplicate topic.
remainingConditions: A decreasing arrangement is an assessment-evidence condition for the same ordering claim. The current examples exercise the other direction; an unillustrated example is not a missing topic or authority to split the ordering claim.

contributions.contribution: Numerals read and written across the selected range, with everyday numerical uses distinguished.

contributions.topicName: The two digits of a two-digit number
contributions.contribution: A two-digit representation interpreted as tens and units using concrete quantities.

records.rationale: The procedural notation claim and conceptual base-ten claim jointly cover the requirement. Their existing evidence includes written symbols and material quantities, rather than rote naming alone.

contributions.contribution: Efficient addition and subtraction with flexible strategies when results remain within one hundred.
Two-digit operands handled with material, pictorial and mental approaches.
A contextual length problem represented and solved using addition or subtraction.

records.rationale: This keeps strategy choice, the two-operand procedure and an actual word-problem application separate. The existing within-one-hundred fluency limit is retained.
remainingConditions: The higher-result fluency and word-problem transfer conditions are not fully evidenced here. This is not authority for another numerical-range or difficulty-level topic: the taxonomy has no separate mastery levels. Review additional examples or a separately justified claim clarification before any semantic change.

contributions.contribution: Equal sets understood through repeated totals.
Equal allocation represented and explained with objects or drawings.

records.rationale: The two conceptual claims explicitly cover the two interpretations required here. Formal table recall and a stronger general multiplication procedure are not added as proxy requirements.

contributions.contribution: Familiar plane figures identified across orientation and size.
Familiar solid figures identified in objects and shape sets.
Figures built from components or drawn.
Figures grouped with stated observable-property criteria.
Object positions described and instructions interpreted with spatial language.

records.rationale: These five independently assessable claims cover identification, construction, property-based grouping and spatial explanation. They retain their complete existing meanings; a shape-name match alone was insufficient.

contributions.contribution: Units selected for length, mass and capacity, followed by actual measurements.
Length instrument chosen to suit the object and used accurately.

records.rationale: Unit selection is directly represented across all selected attributes. Independent instrument choice is explicit for length; the other examples supply a scale or jug without a full choice task.
remainingConditions: Autonomous choice among weighing and volume instruments in the immediate environment remains an observation condition. Using a supplied instrument does not alone establish that choice.

contributions.contribution: Estimate, measure and record short event durations using a supplied suitable timer and an appropriate time unit; actual measurement is assessed separately from reading clock faces.
Dates and event intervals handled using a supplied local calendar.

records.rationale: The time-measurement component is retained on the existing measuring-and-recording claim after separating it from nearest-minute clock reading. The calendar contribution remains unchanged. The same official 3–8 stage window is retained, not a deadline for identical performance at every age. Calendar-fact recall is support, not replacement evidence for measuring an interval.
remainingConditions: An explicit measured interval expressed in months is not established by the selected topic evidence. The larger year/leap-year facts topic is not a substitute for performing that task.

contributions.contribution: Local cash identified by value and features, with equivalent combinations distinguished.
Local unit notation and equivalent amounts interpreted.
Purchase totals and change computed in simple money situations.

records.rationale: The first two claims are explicitly local-currency neutral; their Canadian, Australian and other examples do not restrict them to those jurisdictions. The arithmetic claim is reused without silently replacing its recorded examples.
remainingConditions: The full transaction must still be observed with actual or faithful INR materials within the source limit of INR 100. Numerical money problems and generic coin recognition are component evidence, not proof of that complete local performance.

contributions.contribution: Precise language for quantities, comparisons, figure attributes and positions.

records.rationale: This is a direct mathematical language claim, not a link to general English vocabulary. It does not purport to enumerate all procedural and measurement terminology.
remainingConditions: The measurement-language strand and the breadth of receptive/procedural vocabulary remain unverified by the selected evidence.

contributions.topicName: Using objects to model real problems
contributions.contribution: An everyday quantitative situation represented and a question answered from the model.
A real situation modelled, the result interpreted and a prediction checked or revised.

records.rationale: These are direct modelling and solution activities. They are stronger evidence than generic perseverance or knowing the prerequisite calculations.
remainingConditions: Learner-generated problem formulation and transfer across the full shape/space/measurement range remain open. Representing a supplied situation is not automatically inventing the problem.

records.rationale: Search across Mathematics, Learning to Learn and Personal & Social Development found general persistence, resilience language and Growth Mindset. Knowing those concepts or persevering on an arbitrary task does not demonstrate a mathematics-specific confidence/value attitude.
remainingConditions: No suitable existing mastery claim found in this pass. Decide how domain-specific attitude should be evidenced before proposing a claim; this does not authorize a country-specific duplicate or imply a learner deficit.

partialInterpretation: The nine Partial dispositions are remaining evidence/performance/goal conditions, not nine missing topics. Only C-8.14 is a candidate claim gap, pending a pedagogical decision; no additions or claim changes are authorized by this report.

followUpClaimReconciliation.change: Replace C-8.10 measurement holder UNzo with N55 at the same IN 3–8 stage window; calendar holder unchanged; original 31 links/28 holders and coverage judgments retained.
